content: These references include systematic reviews, meta-analyses, randomized trials, and qualitative studies that explore topics such as antiretroviral therapy (ART) adherence, barriers to care, stigma, and interventions to improve health outcomes for people living with HIV. 1. A mixed-methods study published in PLoS One in 2020 explored the preferences of individuals for different features of HIV services using discrete choice experiments. 2. A 2020 review in Current HIV/AIDS Reports examined the associations between stigma and negative health outcomes for people living with HIV in The Gambia, with a focus on key populations. 3. A study in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes (2015) investigated the intersection of stigma and the health needs of HIV-positive men who have sex with men in Swaziland, emphasizing the importance of dignity and prevention. 4. The WHO's consolidated guidelines on HIV prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care for key populations provide a comprehensive framework for improving health outcomes globally. 5. A systematic review in Social Science & Medicine (2018) analyzed why people living with HIV in lowand middle-income countries delay or avoid initiating treatment, identifying key barriers and facilitators. 6. Research in AIDS Care (2021) highlighted poor linkage to HIV care and low treatment uptake following home-based HIV testing in high-prevalence settings in South Africa. 7. A study in PLoS One (2018) examined the barriers and facilitators to the uptake of test-and-treat strategies in Mozambique, focusing on patient and provider perceptions. 8. A meta-analysis in The Lancet Global Health (2020) compared community-based antiretroviral therapy (ART) delivery with standard clinic-based services in South Africa and Uganda, demonstrating improved outcomes with community-based models. 9. A randomized clinical trial in JAMA (2014) evaluated the impact of optional home initiation of HIV care following self-testing on ART initiation rates in Malawi. 10. A systematic review in AIDS (2018) assessed the benefits and risks of rapid ART initiation, emphasizing the importance of balancing immediate treatment with patient retention. 11. A study in the Journal of International AIDS Society (2020) found that same-day ART initiation in South African public health facilities was associated with increased loss to follow-up. 12. A systematic review in AIDS Behavior (2019) explored the relationship between anxiety and adherence to ART in lowand middle-income countries, highlighting the need for mental health support. 13. A meta-analysis in AIDS Behavior (2018) examined the association between depression and ART adherence, emphasizing the importance of addressing mental health in HIV care. 14. A study in BMC Public Health (2021) investigated the impact of food insecurity on HIV outcomes in Senegal, revealing significant challenges for food-insecure individuals. 15. A systematic review in AIDS Behavior (2012) analyzed the relationship between depression, alcohol use, and ART adherence in sub-Saharan Africa, identifying critical areas for intervention. 16. A review in Pediatrics (2014) discussed the challenges and progress in pediatric drug formulations for HIV treatment, emphasizing the need for child-friendly options. 17. A study in the Annals of Tropical Pediatrics (2011) compared adherence to tablet and liquid formulations of ART among children in Uganda, highlighting the importance of formulation choice. 18. A systematic review in Public Health (2018) identified factors affecting ART adherence among adolescents living with HIV in sub-Saharan Africa, emphasizing the need for tailored interventions. 19. A review in Future Virology (2015) examined the transition of youth living with HIV from pediatric to adult-oriented healthcare, identifying gaps in continuity of care. 20. A systematic review in PLoS One (2014) explored health system barriers and enablers for ART among pregnant and postpartum women, emphasizing the importance of integrated care. 21. A study in AIDS Patient Care and STDs (2011) identified barriers and facilitators to pediatric ART adherence in sub-Saharan Africa, providing insights for improving care delivery. 22. A systematic review in AIDS Behavior (2020) evaluated interventions to improve ART adherence among adolescents and youth in lowand middle-income countries, highlighting effective strategies. 23. A meta-analysis in AIDS (2014) assessed adherence to ART among adolescents living with HIV, identifying key challenges and opportunities for improvement. 24. A study in the Journal of Pediatric Infectious Diseases (2007) examined factors associated with adherence to ART among HIV-infected children and adolescents, emphasizing the role of caregivers and regimen characteristics. 25. A systematic review in AIDS Behavior (2019) analyzed the impact of microfinance interventions on HIV treatment outcomes, proposing a conceptual framework for future research. These rewritten sentences provide a clear and professional summary of the referenced studies, maintaining the integrity of the original content while making it more accessible to a general audience.
